_meta.edition: August 2026 (Ookla computes each monthly edition over a rolling three-month window)
_meta.fields: fixed and mobile are median download speeds in Mbps, as Ookla publishes them to two decimals. month is the edition the fixed figure (or, when fixed is absent, the mobile figure) comes from; mobileMonth is set only when the mobile figure is from a different edition. cities holds Ookla's own city medians, keyed by our city id, only where Ookla publishes that city.
_meta.rules: Latest published edition per metric, taken from each country page (speedtest.net/global-index/<slug>). A metric whose latest edition is older than March 2026 is left null. A metric whose latest value is more than double or less than half the median of the six editions before it is treated as a publication anomaly and left null (Germany mobile, Maldives fixed).

excluded.Maldives: Ookla shows fixed 675 Mbps for May 2026 after 20-37 Mbps in every earlier edition, and no mobile series; no usable figure
excluded.Germany_mobile: 291.96 Mbps in August 2026 against 71-77 Mbps for the prior year, while Berlin's own August median is 144 Mbps; left null

_meta.builtBy: fetched from speedtest.net country pages (embedded var data JSON) and the global index page (city medians); no figure is estimated

noCountryPage.note: Countries and territories in cities-data.js for which speedtest.net/global-index/<slug> returns 404 (every plausible slug tried, 2026-10-01). Ookla publishes no figure for them, so they have no entry.

hongkong.note: Ookla ranks Hong Kong as its own market, not as a city of China; used for the hongkong page in place of the China figures
